sources.finding: Indirect paths default to software cursor composition; this IDD does not opt into hardware cursor support. A controlled standard-arrow reference comparison checks one actual frame. Motion is a separate requirement.

DrawIconEx draws a cursor into a device context. The diagnostic uses an offscreen CPU DIB as a reference, never as the native frame source. A delayed standard-arrow comparison passes exactly; the immediate comparison involved a different hotspot and fails.

The enumeration maps 0 to COMPOSED, 1 to OVERLAY, 2 to NONE and 3 to COMPOSITION_FAILURE. The run reports composed mode during observation and later overlay mode after the observer exits. This temporal association is not a controlled proof of causation or zero GPU cost.

ClipCursor bounds ordinary pointer movement and SetCursorPos. It is shared state that must be released. A future pointer mode needs saved state, independent recovery, and checks under ordinary relative movement; no confinement is claimed in this run.
